--- PDF page 2 ---
How to learn from human data?
• Behavioral Cloning
• Quadratic regret in worst case; bad performance out of expert distribution
• Can’t learn from additional data collected by the agent
• DAgger / TAMER / COACH
• Provides data/feedback on-policy
• Still can’t learn from additional data collected by the agent
• Inverse reinforcement learning
• Infers reward function from demonstrations so that RL can be used

--- PDF page 16 ---
Naive IRL challenges
• RL in the inner loop
• Where do linear features come from?
• Underspeci ed inference problem: in nite reward functions that explain
behavior equally well. Which one to choose?

• Guarantees performance matching, not reward function recovery
• Policies are underspeci ed too: many policies lead to the same
expected features counts. Which one to choose?

• What if demonstrated behavior was actually suboptimal?

fi

fi

fi

• Cannot surpass expert

--- PDF page 17 ---
Suboptimality and policy mixtures
• If a demonstrator acts optimally, then there trivially is some reward function

for which at least one optimal policy exists that matches the demonstrator’s
expected feature counts exactly

• Caveat: the RL step might not nd this policy if there are multiple
optimal policies under the reward function

• But if the demonstrations are sometimes suboptimal, then there may be no
single reward function with this property (aside from degenerate ones e.g.,
all zeros, under which any policy is optimal)

• This can be thought of as the demonstrator acting optimally under di erent

reward functions at di erent times, so a mixture of reward functions (and
their corresponding optimal policies) might be needed to match the mixture
of feature counts

ff

fi

ff

• Thus, the algorithm in Abbeel/Ng returns a mixture policy
